title: Automated remediation and bot-driven dependency updates

videos.script: A lock is safe on the day you compile it. A month later, an advisory names one of its versions. {{stale}} Somebody has to keep proposing the next lock, every week, for ever. That is a job for a bot. {{bots}} This lesson configures two of them, Dependabot and Renovate. You tell them when to ask, how much to group, and how old a release must be before they offer it. {{config}} Dependabot lives on GitHub, so you read its file and have it checked. Renovate runs on your own machine, so you watch it work. {{renovate}} Then a branch with a month-old lock meets an automatic fix. The tool says the fix worked. The pipeline disagrees, and it is right. {{fix}} That is the lesson in one picture. A bot proposes. The pipeline judges. A person decides what goes in. At the end you count a real year of releases for linkbox, and work out how many pull requests a team can actually read. {{count}}
